entry.title: arXiv open questions — 2026-08-20 — 2 papers, 10 questions
entry.content:
arXiv open questions — 2026-08-20

185 new papers, 155 unseen, 155 screened, 2 relevant, 2 kept.

Part 1 — open questions (10, 7 approachable)

  1. The model treats the human ownership share as a single state variable that decays when growth is maximal. What growth rates and consumption rates keep this share stable in an agent-based simulation with heterogeneous firms and agents?
    approachable — Can be written as an agent-based model from the paper's own equations
    from Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
  2. Corporations own populations of AI agents that trade energy, compute, maintenance and upgrades among firms. Does such an inter-corporate market concentrate ownership in a few firms, and under what trading rules?
    approachable — Simulation of trading network plus concentration metrics is self-contained
    from Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
  3. The paper names legal instruments that force the machine economy inside its expansion frontier. Which specific ownership rules, such as mandated dividends or sovereign wealth stakes, actually select the rentier regime rather than full decoupling?
    approachable — Policy rules can be encoded as constraints in the same simulation
    from Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
  4. Growth is claimed to be one to two orders of magnitude higher once agents are manufactured rather than reared. Do measured fabrication throughput and energy capture limits support that range?
    not approachable — Needs proprietary semiconductor and energy capacity data
    from Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
  5. The model assumes AI agents consume energy, compute, maintenance and upgrades. Do current deployed agent systems show any measurable demand for such inputs that behaves like consumption in the model?
    not approachable — Needs internal cost and usage data from agent platform operators
    from Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
  6. Vehicle-to-vehicle cooperation with provenance-aware knowledge graphs is tested against one baseline; how does the method scale as the number of cooperating vehicles grows from a few to hundreds?
    approachable — Open code and driving simulators allow larger fleet runs on modest compute.
    from G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via Knowledge Graphs
  7. Source attribution in shared knowledge graphs assumes honest partners; what happens when some vehicles report false or manipulated object hypotheses?
    approachable — Adversarial agents can be injected into a simulation the researcher writes.
    from G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via Knowledge Graphs
  8. Conflicting evidence between vehicles must be resolved; which resolution rules keep a cooperative fleet stable and avoid correlated failures across all vehicles?
    approachable — Agent-based simulation of shared-evidence dynamics needs no proprietary data.
    from G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via Knowledge Graphs
  9. Structured communication payloads are 25.6x smaller than the baseline; how does performance degrade under realistic message loss and latency in dense traffic?
    approachable — Network delay and dropout models are simple to add to public simulators.
    from G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via Knowledge Graphs
  10. Does the reported gain in occlusion reasoning transfer to road layouts and traffic densities outside the evaluated dataset?
    not approachable — Needs real fleet logs or on-road testing that the profile lacks.
    from G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via Knowledge Graphs

Part 2 — papers (2)

Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
Sahil Sharma
2608.20231 · nearest in your canon: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
Models a post-AGI economy where corporations own producing-and-consuming AI/robot agent populations, using a von Neumann expanding-economy framework. Derives closed-economy demand closure, growth-rate decoupling from human demography, and a golden-rule theorem showing human ownership share decays exponentially unless growth stays below the machine economy's expansion frontier. Characterizes three terminal regimes (rentier post-scarcity, full circular decoupling, socialized ownership) and the policy instruments that select among them.
  • The model treats the human ownership share as a single state variable that decays when growth is maximal. What growth rates and consumption rates keep this share stable in an agent-based simulation with heterogeneous firms and agents? (approachable: Can be written as an agent-based model from the paper's own equations)
  • Corporations own populations of AI agents that trade energy, compute, maintenance and upgrades among firms. Does such an inter-corporate market concentrate ownership in a few firms, and under what trading rules? (approachable: Simulation of trading network plus concentration metrics is self-contained)
  • The paper names legal instruments that force the machine economy inside its expansion frontier. Which specific ownership rules, such as mandated dividends or sovereign wealth stakes, actually select the rentier regime rather than full decoupling? (approachable: Policy rules can be encoded as constraints in the same simulation)
  • Growth is claimed to be one to two orders of magnitude higher once agents are manufactured rather than reared. Do measured fabrication throughput and energy capture limits support that range? (not approachable: Needs proprietary semiconductor and energy capacity data)
  • The model assumes AI agents consume energy, compute, maintenance and upgrades. Do current deployed agent systems show any measurable demand for such inputs that behaves like consumption in the model? (not approachable: Needs internal cost and usage data from agent platform operators)
G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via Knowledge Graphs
Bhavya Gupta, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing
2608.19964 · nearest in your canon: Habermolt: Delegating Deliberation to AI Representatives
Proposes G-MARK, a framework converting cooperative vehicle-to-vehicle perception data into provenance-aware knowledge graphs for occlusion reasoning and planning. Reports improved occlusion reasoning accuracy, reduced control-selection error, and smaller communication payload versus a baseline on cooperative driving tasks.
  • Vehicle-to-vehicle cooperation with provenance-aware knowledge graphs is tested against one baseline; how does the method scale as the number of cooperating vehicles grows from a few to hundreds? (approachable: Open code and driving simulators allow larger fleet runs on modest compute.)
  • Source attribution in shared knowledge graphs assumes honest partners; what happens when some vehicles report false or manipulated object hypotheses? (approachable: Adversarial agents can be injected into a simulation the researcher writes.)
  • Conflicting evidence between vehicles must be resolved; which resolution rules keep a cooperative fleet stable and avoid correlated failures across all vehicles? (approachable: Agent-based simulation of shared-evidence dynamics needs no proprietary data.)
  • Structured communication payloads are 25.6x smaller than the baseline; how does performance degrade under realistic message loss and latency in dense traffic? (approachable: Network delay and dropout models are simple to add to public simulators.)
  • Does the reported gain in occlusion reasoning transfer to road layouts and traffic densities outside the evaluated dataset? (not approachable: Needs real fleet logs or on-road testing that the profile lacks.)
